title: Russell US Style indexes — conditional MONTH-end recapping effective at the open (24% / 4.8%-above-48% test struck on the 2026-10-27 close), the first untracked instance of a check the owner's guide made monthly
source: EST: owner-published, read direct this session. FTSE Russell, "Capping Methodology Guide", v5.4, September 2026 (lseg.com dam policy-documents, capping-methodology-guide.pdf, HTTP 200, 652,008 bytes, 62 content streams inflated 2026-09-08). Its section 4.8.6 table lists every Russell US Style index with frequency "Monthly", price date "T-3", effective date "Last business day of each month", trigger "No company is greater than 24%, and all companies that have a weight greater than 4.8% in aggregate are no more than 48% of the index", scheme "Rule 4.2/RIC 22.5/45". CORROBORATED IN A SECOND, INDEPENDENTLY ARCHIVED EDITION: v5.3, August 2026, recovered from web.archive.org (snapshot 2026-09-02) and inflated in-session, carries identical wording for the same rows. THE DATE IS ARITHMETIC FROM THE STANDING RULE, NOT A PUBLISHED CALENDAR ENTRY: the last business day of October 2026 is Friday 30 October, so the effective date is 2026-10-30 and T-3 is Tuesday 2026-10-27 (T-1 Thu 29 Oct, T-2 Wed 28 Oct; no exchange holiday intervenes). Filed estimate on four counts, one of which is a genuine conflict a later lane must not read as settled: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy has no member for an index owner's published methodology; this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep; the date is derived from a standing rule rather than read off the owner's dated schedule table, which publishes only the four quarter-end instances; and THE OWNER'S OWN JULY 2026 FAQ CONTRADICTS THE GUIDE, saying verbatim "The review is conducted quarterly (March, June, September, and December)". Conditional by construction -- "If no breach is identified, no changes are made." Discovered during the russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-12-31 initial research, checked 2026-09-08
notes: PROPOSED by the russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-12-31 initial research (2026-09-08), alongside proposals/russell-style-month-end-capping-effective-2026-11-30.from-russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-12-31.json -- the two month-end instances between that research's session and the event it was researching. WHY IT EXISTS AT ALL: the December lane had to establish the check's frequency before it could price the December instance, and found that this calendar's model of the family -- four quarter-end instances a year -- descends from a July 2026 FAQ that the owner's own methodology guide has since superseded. Between the June 2026 (v5.2) and August 2026 (v5.3) editions, every Russell US Style row in the guide's section 4.8.6 table changed from "Last business day in Mar, Jun, Sep and Dec" to frequency "Monthly" / "Last business day of each month". The quarterly wording that survives in v5.4 belongs to the two FTSE Emerging ex China rows two lines above the Russell ones -- which is also the misattribution the sibling ledger russell-style-quarter-end-capping-effective-2026-09-30 recorded as fact. If the guide governs, this family runs TWELVE conditional recapping checks a year across about $294.6B of iShares assets (IWF, IWD, IWY, IWX, IWP, IWS, IWO, IWN) and the calendar tracks four. THIS IS THE EARLIER OF THE TWO FILED, and it is the more informative one for exactly one reason: it is the FIRST month-end instance that is not also a quarter-end, so whether anything happens on 2026-10-30 is the cleanest available test of whether the monthly reading is right. If FTSE Russell publishes no index notice around 2026-10-27/30 and the capped indexes show no recapping, the FAQ's quarterly wording is probably still what the owner operates, and both this entry and its November sibling should be withdrawn rather than researched. The 2027 instances were DELIBERATELY DECLINED -- no owner document published this session names a 2027 date, and extrapolating a standing rule twelve months out is calendar noise, not foresight. WHAT THE PROPOSING RESEARCH'S VERDICT WAS, travelling with the proposal so nobody sizes this as tradable: stand aside. Comparable measured breach probability is single-digit -- from a 45% reset the cohort must beat its own index by 6.67%, which cleared 96 of 1,237 rolling 17-session windows (7.76%, IWY cohort) and 111 of 1,237 (8.97%, IWF cohort) across five years of real prices. The single-name leg is dead by a wide margin (NVDA 16.21% in IWY against a 24% trigger), five of the eight funds carry no constituent within reach of 4.8%, and a fired recap moves about 3pp of IWY's $15.94B -- roughly $478M -- across five of the most liquid names on the tape. Impact low and symbols deliberately EMPTY on the same measured grounds as both quarter-end entries. Kind sector matches the family.
